builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: From Watching to Steering: Enabling Human-Coding Agent Collaboration through Execution Traces
summary: It replaces conventional log-based interaction and full run restarts with interactive execution-trace visualization, mid-run forking, and distillation of traces plus human feedback into reusable skills. It costs a custom instrumentation and UI layer built on OpenCode, ongoing human supervision time, and added system complexity. It can fail if distilled skills overfit to past tasks, if traces become too long to inspect reliably on long runs, or if forked executions diverge from validated state in subtle ways.
rationale: The token and cost savings are plausible at single-GPU or API scale, but the gains depend on the reader's specific coding-agent workload and the OpenCode-based stack must be integrated and validated before production adoption.
technique: Interactive agent execution traces with forking and skill distillation

claims.statement: It replaces conventional log-based interaction and full run restarts with interactive execution-trace visualization, mid-run forking, and distillation of traces plus human feedback into reusable skills. It costs a custom instrumentation and UI layer built on OpenCode, ongoing human supervision time, and added system complexity. It can fail if distilled skills overfit to past tasks, if traces become too long to inspect reliably on long runs, or if forked executions diverge from validated state in subtle ways.
Distilled skills reduce input tokens by 23.0% and cost by 15.5%, and improve SWE-bench Verified pass rate from 65.0% to 68.0%.
